heading: Held-out language-model loss follows power laws when other resources are sufficient
definition: held-out pretraining loss of language models falls as a power law in parameters, tokens or compute when the other two are not the bottleneck, over several orders of magnitude.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce power-law loss scaling within tested training recipes and the curve shapes used in their fits, including models spanning 111M–13B parameters. Independent reproduction above 100B parameters remains unestablished.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at <1B, 1-10B and 10-100B for tested recipes and fitted forms; ? at >100B for independent reproduction of the stated loss law.
suggested_status.reason: Cerebras-GPT reports held-out Pile loss scaling across 111M–13B models with co-scaled tokens (arXiv:2304.03208#R1,#R7,#R11,#R12). Supervised µP Transformers on C4 independently supply joint parameter/token validation-loss fits across 143M–12.6B with approximately 1% or less relative error (arXiv:2502.08606#r1). These support R2 within their conditions. counts: versions.V1.studies_by_size and versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size record coverage through >100B, but coverage alone does not establish replication quality. GPT-3 reports a qualitative compute trend with fixed tokens (arXiv:2005.14165#R1); OPT supplies qualitative within-run perplexity trajectories without a fitted loss law (arXiv:2212.09803#R6). Neither establishes independent parameter/token laws above 100B under demonstrated non-bottleneck conditions.
suggested_status.open_questions: Independent >100B training sweeps with held-out cross-entropy, quantified functional-form comparisons and demonstrated complementary-resource sufficiency would establish the large-scale level. Controlled GPT2/GitHub replication with matched training histories and verified evaluation splits would determine whether the recorded challenges persist.

source.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
source.authors: Jared Kaplan; Sam McCandlish; Tom Henighan; Tom B. Brown; Benjamin Chess; Rewon Child; Scott Gray; Alec Radford; Jeffrey Wu; Dario Amodei

original_result.setup: Kaplan et al. varied Transformer size, WebText2 training data and compute, measuring test cross-entropy.
original_result.result: Separate power-law fits gave exponents of approximately 0.076 for non-embedding parameters, 0.095 for tokens and 0.057 for fixed-batch compute. Adjusting for batch-size efficiency gave a compute exponent of approximately 0.050.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

wording_issues.issue: The µP width study measures online training cross-entropy versus width; MDM-Prime-v2 and the variational-decoding AR suite also measure training loss. The AR suite spans 33.8M–1.08B non-embedding parameters, with no AR 3B run. These measurements leave V1's held-out-loss requirement untested. SuperValid reports a qualitative trend in synthetic capability-aligned OOD cross-entropy over 10M–324M active parameters, without fitted exponents; this does not establish V1's pretraining-loss law or its stated scale range. Withholding model configurations does not establish a held-out text split.

Successful forms often describe reducible loss above a floor or sum parameter/data power terms, as in Chinchilla. LaMDA's pure-law estimator fits poorly without an asymptote. The cMoLLM size sweep establishes decreasing validation loss without a power-law fit; the Polish ladder's three-parameter fit through three points leaves no residual for assessing the form. These size comparisons leave V1's functional form and several-orders regime untested, rather than demonstrating partial scaling or a departure.

MLP Memory fits perplexity, which does not establish a power law in cross-entropy. The discrete-diffusion fits measure training negative ELBO without a stated held-out evaluation, leaving V1 untested. Neurograf reports BPB. The reservoir study fits minimum loss against log10 parameter count rather than a power law in loss; its text and caption identify training loss while its plot title and axis identify testing loss. That split is unresolved, and the fitted form neither establishes nor refutes V1.

Capacity coordinates include total versus active MoE parameters, expert count and effective unrolled parameters. The MoE configuration study obtains different fit quality with total and active parameters; routed-model expert sweeps and Parcae's recurrence-aware fits require their reported coordinates. The µP width sweep instead fits online training cross-entropy versus network width. It illustrates a different coordinate and target, leaving V1's held-out-loss law in parameters, tokens or compute untested.

Co-scaled ladders in the hypersphere-optimization and variable-width studies describe compute trajectories without separately identifying parameter and token laws. The dynamic-time study uses a transformed time coordinate. Learning-rate-annealing fits include a history correction, so their full-equation fit quality does not independently validate an uncorrected token law.

wording_issues.phrase: when the other two are not the bottleneck
wording_issues.issue: The qualification is unresolved in these settings. BitNet fixes training tokens while increasing model size, with the total unspecified. The synthetic-PCFG masked-model plateau occurs at fixed model size without verified complementary-resource sufficiency. Fixed-size byte-model curvature is attributed to capacity limits. JASMINE reports equal steps without per-model token budgets; its decreasing perplexities do not establish a loss power law or departure. These unresolved conditions do not establish an additional limitation or failure of V1.

wording_issues.phrase: when the other two are not the bottleneck
wording_issues.issue: Parameters, tokens and compute do not exhaust the observed conditions. TinyStories/WikiText and character-level experiments show context-dependent saturation. nanoLM's parameterization and hyperparameter sensitivity concerns training-loss fits, supporting V7 while leaving V1's held-out-loss requirement untested; µP is sufficient but not necessary for those scaling laws. Random model shapes worsen the parameter/token-only fit in the inference-efficiency study.

Some linked results cover only local behavior. Recipe-asymptote data fits span 200M–1.6B seed tokens; the MoE data sweep spans 10B–50B tokens; the efficient-attention study fits small sizes with a separate verification size. MatGPT reports lower validation loss at 6.7B than at 1.7B with the same tokenization and vocabulary, without establishing a power-law form or exponent. These results do not individually establish the stated range; MatGPT's comparison leaves the functional form untested as well.

Family, training distribution and evaluation domain distinguish the reported results. Both cross-family evaluation studies report poor GPT2 cross-entropy power-law fits on their GitHub conditions, with uncontrolled training histories. Llama follows a different but qualitatively similar parameter-loss path from GPT-2/OPT/BLOOM; no fitted form establishes a V1 limitation, and V1 does not require a common curve across families. Uniform synthetic knowledge data produce departures from power-law data scaling, supporting V7's setup dependence while showing absent V1 behavior in those conditions.

Some supporting settings use speech tokens, continuous speech representations, protein sequences or molecular strings. These extend sequence-model coverage but differ in data distribution or objective from natural-language text pretraining.

method_sensitivity.factor: Functional form, loss floor, regression and fit window
method_sensitivity.what: The Chinchilla reconstruction reports sensitivity to rounding, optimizer behavior and low-D/N outliers; D/N<0.4 observations do not establish V1's non-bottleneck condition. LaMDA validation loss is rescaled to [0,1]; asymptotic estimators M2/M4 give exponents near −1/3 and outperform M1/M3. Extrapolation is scored by RMSE of log rescaled loss; exact estimator-specific Table 2 values remain unresolved. Chinchilla reanalysis excludes the smallest-D observations, whereas Farseer excludes the highest-loss observations; both target insufficiently trained, non-asymptotic observations. The fault-free FineWeb study changes its estimated parameter exponent when the fixed loss floor changes.

Enoki's 45.7M–2.62B ladder has systematic single-law curvature under Chinchilla 6N accounting but single saturated-law R²=0.9997–0.9998 under Kaplan 6P; these qualify V1 under 6N and support it under 6P. Uniform diffusion's smoothed training-negative-ELBO compute exponent changes from −0.05219 under Method 1 to −0.04903 under Method 2's M=6P approximation; held-out loss is not established. Architecture-search results show that embeddings can obscure decoder-parameter/perplexity rankings, without establishing a power-law form. Precision-aware fitting substitutes effective parameters and constrains parameter/data exponents to equality.

Cerebras reports relative residual SD around the SP scaling fit of 0.66% for SP at 111M–13B versus 0.04% for µP at 111M–2.7B. nanoLM's tested standard-parametrization settings give poorer training-loss power-law fits, and off-basin transferred hyperparameters generalize poorly; µP is sufficient but unnecessary, and held-out V1 behavior is untested. Size-specific OpenLM optimizer tuning changes curved compute frontiers into saturated-law fits; the Kaplan reproduction uses smoothed training loss. On 50M–1.5B optimizer sweeps, independent Chinchilla fits have errors around 1e-5; imposing AdamW reference exponents raises errors to approximately 3e-4 while retaining reported good fit. Table 2 leaves the model family unspecified and does not establish pooled OLMo-2/LLaMa fitting. Optimizer-dependent residuals demonstrate V7 sensitivity without establishing a V1 limitation.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning-rate history, batch size, convergence and time coordinate
method_sensitivity.what: Annealing and re-warmup require a learning-rate-history correction to step-only loss laws: partial V1 behavior and observed V7 sensitivity. Later Pythia aggregate cross-model collapse, after separately fitting constants, improves from R²=0.93 against steps to 0.98 against dynamic time τ. This does not show that individual step/token laws fail; with varying learning rates, τ is nonlinear in steps/tokens and its law does not directly establish V1. Constant-learning-rate Llama-2 runs support a cumulative-learning-rate power law, while comparisons across decay schedules require additional schedule terms. Fixed-164M token-scaling fits vary across batch-size/scheduler settings, with reported R² from 0.9613 to 0.9970.

method_sensitivity.factor: Data distribution, evaluation domain and model-family pooling
method_sensitivity.what: Observational GPT2 cross-entropy fits fail on corpora labeled GitHub: R²=0.0717 in the cross-entropy decomposition study and 0.091 in the relative-scaling study. Their other evaluation domains have stronger fits; pooling families also weakens fits in the decomposition study. Poor fit is absent V1 behavior and contributes to observed V7 setup dependence. PALOMA and specialized-mixture experiments show domain-specific loss increasing with additional training tokens while aggregate loss or other domains improve. PALOMA's two-point slopes do not establish power-law form; worsening domains reverse V1's decreasing-loss direction while demonstrating V7 sensitivity. Training data, tokenizers and training lengths are uncontrolled in the family comparisons.

method_sensitivity.factor: Data repetition, density, overtraining and pretraining history
method_sensitivity.what: Repeated-data fraction and frequency change parameter-law departures and within-run plateaus or reversals. Parameter-law departures and 50%-repeated-token plateaus limit V1; rising loss at 90% repeated tokens and approximately 100x–10,000x repetition challenges its decreasing-loss direction. These are observed V7 sensitivity. Data-density experiments report overtraining-ratio-dependent training-loss compute exponents before stabilization at larger ratios; these exponent rows do not establish held-out V1 behavior. Effective-resource fits under repeated-data constraints change with fitting stage, with weaker second-step AR fits than initial AR fits; they test V5 rather than V1's non-bottleneck scaling in actual resources. Second-stage pretraining laws depend on first-stage token budget, checkpoint phase and reuse/growth configuration; interaction terms change the effective second-stage exponent.

method_sensitivity.factor: Model shape, routing structure, recurrence and capacity placement
method_sensitivity.what: Randomizing model shape raises parameter/token-only fit MSE from 0.0033 to 0.0198; adding a shape term gives MSE 0.0008 under random shapes. MoE fit R² changes from 0.641 with active parameters alone to 0.985 with total parameters and expert/routing terms. Iso-depth looped-Transformer parameter and token exponents depend on recurrence. Truncated-backpropagation results depend on the recurrence-to-effective-capacity mapping and training recipe; its 230-configuration fitting set includes 226 configurations from the five-size grid and four compute-matched configurations, including additional sizes 79M and 162M.

TinyStories/WikiText data-scaling fits break down when the effective learning horizon approaches context length; adding later data points can lower the fitted exponent. Character-level tinyShakespeare and WikiText-103 curves saturate at context-dependent loss levels, with longer contexts delaying saturation. The context-dependent saturation is partial V1 behavior and observed V7 sensitivity.

method_sensitivity.factor: Tokenization, objective and loss evaluation protocol
method_sensitivity.what: Latent and subword C4 BPB compute fits have exponents −0.206 and −0.181; Table 1 reports no latent confidence intervals. The subword sweep covers 1×10^19–2×10^21 FLOPs. Arithmetic-coded C4 streams show no model-size improvement, unlike learnable tokenizations; decreasing loss alone does not establish a power law, and the largest models remain undertrained. StaticAC[v=256]'s uniform baseline is 4.62 bits/byte in Table 15; its 25m model gives 4.61. The same MDM checkpoints give compute exponents −0.0623 under ELBO and −0.0659 under DUEL exact likelihood with top-1 confidence unmasking. Fixed approximately 1B supervised token/byte models at learning rate 4e-3 on Validation dataset 1 have saturating BPB compute exponents −0.500369 and −0.365844.

Low-precision floating-point fits require an additional precision-dependent loss term; Figure 8a's predicted-versus-actual alignment concerns training loss and does not establish held-out V1 behavior. OLMo fits depend on stable precision settings and forward/backward quantization choices. Joint OLMo2 BF16/W4A4 fits at D/N=20 use rho_BF16=1 and fitted rho_4bit; exponents vary by optimizer. AdamW spans 50M–1.5B; PSGD and SOAP use 50M, 125M, 350M, 500M and 760M, with no reported 1.5B results. Spectra 1.1 ternary and FloatLM suites have different fitted parameter/data exponents; their reported fit quality is in-sample over narrow ranges.
